message.content: {"36": {"original": "Leasing products or using vague 'software-as-a-service' models is wrong because ", "rephrased": "When companies lease products or utilize the vague concept of software-as-a-service, they deny users the ability to control the software running on their own devices, a practice that must be replaced by models where users run free programs themselves to ensure genuine ownership and control.", "summary": "Leasing products or vague service models deny users control over software, necessitating a shift to user-run free programs."}, "37": {"original": "Company claims of limited licenses are mistreatment of the public.", "rephrased": "Corporate assertions that software purchases grant only limited licenses rather than true ownership constitute a fundamental mistreatment of the public, as this approach denies users the right to freely use, modify, and share the programs they have paid for.", "summary": "Corporate limited licenses constitute a fundamental mistreatment of the public by denying users true ownership rights."}, "38": {"original": "Software must be free to grant users four essential freedoms: run, study, copy, ", "rephrased": "To protect user rights, all software must be free, guaranteeing four essential freedoms: the liberty to run the program for any purpose, the right to study and modify the source code, the freedom to make exact copies, and the ability to distribute modified versions to others.", "summary": "All software must be free to guarantee users four essential freedoms: running, studying, copying, and sharing."}, "39": {"original": "Freedom to resell copies involves making new copies, not just transferring the ", "rephrased": "The freedom to resell software copies involves the right to create and distribute new copies rather than merely transferring the original, ensuring that users can legally share or sell the program itself without being restricted by the company's initial distribution terms.", "summary": "The freedom to resell software involves creating new copies, ensuring users can legally share or sell the program."}}
